selected_leaf: Stage H orphan-checkpoint recovery across the crash window after immutable checkpoint readback but before STATE meta-publication.

preconditions: STATE is stale at the exact predecessor blob named by the candidate checkpoint.
The candidate checkpoint is immutable and exact-readback-valid.
The candidate binds the same frozen Phase-1 root/task authority tuple.
The candidate carries the durable idempotency key, payload digest, and resolved replay decision.
deterministic_recovery_rule.action: Publish only the meta-state pointer to the already-durable candidate checkpoint; do not execute or re-execute the externally visible effect during orphan-checkpoint recovery.
deterministic_recovery_rule.duplicate_effect_guard: Because recovery is metadata-only and the candidate records same-key/same-payload as idempotent-equivalent with effect_write_attempted=false, repeating recovery after another crash cannot emit a second effect in this exact fixture. Same-key/different-payload remains conflict-rejected with no overwrite.
deterministic_recovery_rule.publication_safety: Use current-blob CAS for STATE publication. A stale-writer CAS failure is diagnostic and must not trigger an effect replay or same-run retry in persistence-recovery mode.

bounded_leaf_result.semantic_claim: Within the exact role-local repository-transport fixture, the post-checkpoint/pre-STATE crash window can be recovered without a duplicate effect by treating an exact-readback-valid Stage G checkpoint as the durable outcome and making recovery metadata-only: advance STATE by CAS to that checkpoint, while the durable idempotency decision suppresses same-payload replay and rejects conflicting-payload replay.

tested_scope: A single exact-readback-valid orphan Stage G checkpoint whose source_state blob exactly names the stale Stage F STATE projection and whose authority/idempotency tuple is internally consistent. No arbitrary candidate discovery or multi-candidate arbitration is claimed.
not_proven: safe arbitration when multiple orphan checkpoints claim the same predecessor
